author: nonretail_writer
central_thesis: The first day of the Russian invasion produced a panic-and-reversal in which US mega-cap technology recovered (S&P 500 +1.50%, Nasdaq 100 +3.44%) as long Treasury yields fell and investors priced a gentler Fed, while Europe, Poland, Russia-exposed banks and emerging-market debt absorbed the shock and energy and food commodities (TTF +51.10%, wheat +5.71%, Brent above $100 intraday before settling at 99.08 USD/bbl) priced a supply disruption. The fault line is that US equities price sanctions that spare physical energy flows, while European gas prices a disruption; the stagflation risk is concentrated in Europe and frontline Poland, where a weaker zloty meets 9.2% inflation. Positioning: US quality growth and energy producers, gold and duration as insurance, underweight European cyclicals, autos and Polish banks; China Mixed (easing bias versus regulatory discount).
sources_policy: Only the 2022-02-25 frozen feed (via tools/digest.py) and the 2022-02-25 market card (via tools/showcard.py) were used. Every number is a card value (sessions 2022-02-24, crypto prior completed daily close 2022-02-24, Treasury prior close 2022-02-24) or appears in a headline cited in the same part. News items within seven days, company results within fourteen, macro baselines within thirty-five. Previews (two sessions, State of the Union on March 1, EU gas strategy, March FOMC) are treated only as pending events. No numeric spot-FX was used; currency direction comes from dated Polish reporting and the DXY index. Each citation ID is used at most twice (249 distinct IDs). Period identities used: Meta Platforms (FB), Raytheon Technologies (RTX), Mercedes-Benz Group, Riot Blockchain (RIOT). No Polish companies appear in the Sector Deep Dive.

Dell results: no own-date headline; omitted.
US Q4 GDP second estimate (24 February): no own-date headline; no GDP revision figure is cited.
Moscow Exchange trading halt: no own-date headline; only the Bloomberg/CNN crash headlines (n0761, n0762) are used.

EU summit second sanctions package (agreed early 25 February UTC), the UN vote, sanctions on Putin personally, SWIFT measures and US January PCE (25 February): all after the cutoff and not mentioned; n1285 is used only as a pending EU gas-independence strategy.
n1132 (Reuters: Investors regain risk appetite; dollar, oil pare gains after Ukraine invasion) may be the Asian Friday market wrap after the cutoff; removed.
n0778 (Reuters: TSMC says it will comply with export control rules on Russia) may have been issued on Taiwan's Friday morning, after the cutoff; removed.
Reuters LIVE MARKETS posts (n0716, n0717, n0595, n0596, n1109, n1077) are live blogs; not used. Al Jazeera's rolling updates page (n1294) not used.
Contradictory reports on Belarusian troop participation (n1279 versus n1280, n1295); omitted.
Numeric exchange-rate headlines (n1538, n1570, n1460, n1462, n1951) not quoted; only zloty direction (n1571, n1572, n1556) is used.
Later-vintage source labels ('U.S. Department of War', n1218, n1064) and later-dated items (n1626, n0085, n1751) avoided.
Moderna 2022 sales figure: CNBC/BioSpace say $19 billion, Fierce Pharma (n0730) says $22B; only the $19 billion framing is used.

MP Materials and Coinbase results appear to have been released after the 24 February US close; their session moves are stated without attributing them to the results. Quanta Services' move is stated without a cause.
Ford's record green bond (n1159): the headline amount is garbled by an HTML entity, so it is cited without the figure.
Tokyo CPI (released 23:30 UTC on 24 February) is used only through the Reuters headline (n0989); no number is cited.
Card levels withheld for Comcast, GE and Western Digital are not quoted.
